text.p: On overnight commodity markets, copper and aluminium prices drifted lower London in quiet May Day trade.
Gold prices edged a touch higher on fund short-covering, but continued to lanquish around US$340 an ounce.
Oil prices edged lower on NYMEX, but there were few major factors.
Wheat prices fell on a technical slide on bullish production news of rain in the Great plains.
The CRB index closed down 0.39 at 247.90.
LME copper and aluminium drifted lower in sluggish activity on Thursday afternoon, but the markets were well-underpinned and only pausing, traders and analysts said.

Turnover was light due to the May Day holiday in much of Europe and the Golden Week celebrations in Japan. Britain observes a holiday on Monday, May 5, so LME activity is likely to be muted on Friday as well.

Three months copper finished the afternoon kerb $19 weaker at $2,360 a tonne after failing to sustain a move in the morning to $2,382. The premium of cash over three months material eased to $75/$80 from about $88 on Wednesday evening.

Traders said the downside was limited due to the backwardation and supply side difficulties. A small group of miners at Chile's huge Escondida mine were on strike, as were workers at Quebrada Blanca, another Chilean mine.
Aluminium also ended weaker after failing at $1,647 in the morning. It lost $17 to end the day at $1,628.
Support was pegged at a chart gap at $1,614-$1,620.
The others were lacklustre, holding to recent ranges.
Nickel fell $30 to $7,350, while zinc lost $4 to $1,269.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures recovered from some early weakness to end higher Thursday on moderate volumes, helped by some shortcovering by locals and funds, traders said. COMEX June gold ended up 50 cents at $341.70 an ounce, after seeing a $340.40-342.90 range.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $340.15/65 midday, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $339.25 and the New York close Wednesday around $339.30/80.
NYMEX crude ended lower Thursday after a lack of buying interest at slimly firmer levels sparked late session profit-taking on thin volume.

June crude ended 30 cents a barrel lower at $19.91 after hovering a few cents higher within a tight $20.21 to $20.25 price range most of the day. On the charts, technicians had been predicting June crude to break out of a bearish wedge formation on the spot continuation chart.

CBOT wheat futures closed lower on a profit taking technical slide with rain forecasts for portions of the drier U.S. Great Plains and signs of showers in key European wheat areas also mentioned, traders said.

Weather patterns suggested some potential relief for the crop in drier areas of the U.S. and in France. USDA's weekly export sales report underpinned prices. USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended April 24 totaled 290,500 tonnes, above trade expectations for 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 to nine cents per bushel lower, with July down nine 8-1/2 cents at $4.25.
